title: Ide tribe names
description: The clan and lineage names, and what each one means.
html:
A

Abamba — Someone who cannot be scolded.

Abatam / Abata — I have arrived.

Achi na uwa na ike/Achike — Do not rule the world by force.

Adaeze — The wealthy/King’s daughter.

Adanna / Adannia — Father’s first daughter.

Adanze — The chief’s daughter.

Adaobi — The king’s daughter.

Adaora — The people’s daughter.

Adaugo — Daughter of an eagle (glory).

Adanwuzo — First daughter who owns the path.

Adi n’igwe/Adigwe — If we are numerous, we will win.

Afam / Afamefune — My name shall not be lost.

Afunwa elote nna / lotenna — When you see the child, you remember the father.

Afunwa elote nne / lotenne — When you see the child, you remember the mother.

Agbeke — Female child born on eke day.

Agbafo — Female child born on afo day.

Agbala — Goddess of fertility (signifies power and strength).

Agbankwo — Female child born on nkwo day.

Agboye — Female child born on oye day.

Agaku / Duaku — Master of wealth.

Agwabumma / Bumma — Character is beauty.

Aguiyi — Crocodile

Agunwa / Agunwo — Leopard’s child.

Akajiagu — The hand that holds the leopard.

Akala — Deity of Power.

Akalaka — Destiny.

Akana ife uwa na anya/Akanya/Akana — Allow things to go by sequence; do not brag.

Akazue — The hand is full.

Akobundu / Ako — Wisdom is life.

Akoli — There is wisdom.

Akonso — Holy wisdom.

Akoana — Wisdom of the land.

Akouwa — Wisdom of the world.

Akuabata — Wealth has arrived.

Akuana — Wealth of the land.

Akububa / Akuba — Wealth is massive.

Akuliuba — There is massive wealth.

Akudo — Peaceful wealth.

Akuelike — Wealth is a lot/too much

Akuenwebe — Wealth has no home

Akuezue — Wealth is complete.

Akuibe — Joint wealth.

Akujiobi — Wealth gives confidence.

Akulienne — When wealth is too much.

Aku m bu n’alu / Bunalu — The wealth I am carrying.

Akumefune — May my wealth not be lost.

Akunata — Wealth should return.

Akunna / Akunnia — Father’s wealth.

Akunne / Akunnie — Mother’s wealth.

Akuose — God’s wealth

Anabaluose / Abadom — A plea not to be chastised (Reference to a family previously traduced).

Anachebe — May Mother God keep us safe.

Anachebem / Chebem — May the land protect me.

Anadum / Anadu — May the land lead me.

Anaekwensi / Ekwensi — May the earth prevent the charm.

Anaeto — The land praises you.

Anaeze — Land of wealth.

Anaka — Branch (can imply God’s branch).

Anakadibia / Anaka — Mother God is greater than the priest.

Anamanda / Amanda — The land won’t fall.

Anamefune / Aname — May my land not be lost.

Ananso — Holy land.

Anaose / Anose — God’s land.

Anapuwa — If they take the world.

Ana raa / Araa — A plea for Mother Earth's protection.

Anaweteli — The land brought it.

Anazaa m / Zaa / Zaam — Mother God answered me.

Ayondu — beginning of life

Azaka — obedient

Azikiwe — Curse is greater than anger (It is better to be angry at me than to curse me).

Azubueze — Family pedigree is wealth.

Emenike — Not by one's strength.

Emenjo / Emenenjo — Do not commit evil.

Eziakala — Good power

Ezike — Good strength.

Ezindu — Good life.

Feekugo / Fekugo — Fly like an eagle.

Gbamnwa — A complete child.

Gbuzue — Kill completely.

ezeoko — King of money.

Ideugo — Glorious king.

Iveadigo / Adigo — Things are better (Light has come).

Ifediba — Let there be light.

Ifedimma — Light is good.

Ivemelinamma / Ivemeli — Things done with beauty.

Iveukwu — Great things.
